highcharter

Highcharter brings Highcharts to R. Turn data frames, time series and statistical results into interactive visualizations, explore geographic data and create financial charts with a flexible R interface.

Installation

Install from CRAN:

install.packages("highcharter")

Or install the development version from GitHub:

remotes::install_github("jbkunst/highcharter")

What’s included

One Highcharts bundle brings together Charts, Stock, Maps and Gantt. Choose from dozens of chart types and combine them with tooltips, zoom, drilldown, annotations, exporting and accessibility features.

  • Chart R objects with hchart(): data frames, vectors, time series, forecasts and survival models all have a starting point.
  • Create choropleths with hcmap() and bring your own geographic data.
  • Explore financial time series and candlesticks with highchartstock(), technical indicators and Stock Tools.
  • Make charts your own with themes, colors, labels and languages.
  • Add interactive charts to Shiny applications and R Markdown documents.

Where to start

  • First steps: create your first chart from a data frame.
  • hchart() guide: chart time series, forecasts and other R objects.
  • Showcase: discover ideas for customization and chart design.
  • Chart types: find a chart type and its R example.
  • Maps and Stock charts and Stock Tools: explore places and financial time series.
  • Shiny and accessibility: build interactive experiences for your audience.
  • Function reference: look up helpers and chart options.
  • Highcharts API in R and JavaScript-to-R guide: learn how Highcharts options translate to R code.

Licensing

The R wrapper in highcharter is licensed under MIT. Every chart created with highcharter uses the bundled Highcharts JavaScript library. Your use of Highcharts must be covered by the applicable Highsoft terms for commercial use or personal and educational use.
